source.check: Votes as printed: 'Francis M'Connell 730; Thomas C. Gormley, 501. Majority for M'Connell 229.' 730-501=229. Original citation restored 6 Nov 2026 (the 5 Nov verification had moved it because of a text-cleaning fault).

note: Triennial election of Tyrone County Council. Nominations were received on 17 May 1949 and polling in contested divisions was fixed for 'Thursday, June 2', with the results announced the following day (Belfast News-Letter, 18 May 1949, p. 7). The only contest was in Plumbridge, where Francis M'Connell (Nat.) polled 730 and Thomas C. Gormley (Nat.) 501 (Irish News, 4 June 1949, p. 3). The Ulster Herald of 11 June 1949 prints the Returning Officer's notice of result for the county, which lists all 27 divisions; the 26 uncontested members are recorded from it. Uncontested divisions here reflect a deliberate abstention, not missing coverage: in the Omagh Rural District, Nationalists refused to nominate against Unionist-held seats in every year except 1949, when only 4 of 21 such seats were contested (Kingsley 2021, 'The Omagh Rural District Electoral Divisions Scheme 1923', citing PRONI LA/62/2/FA/38 and Ulster Herald 10 Feb 1923). See notes/tyrone-county-council_absent_contests.txt Both candidates were Nationalists and the paper notes that the voting was not on political lines.
